definition: A sentence structure in which the subject performs the action expressed by the verb.
use_cases: The dog chased the cat. (active voice)
She wrote the letter. (active voice, clearer and more direct than passive)

definition: A sentence structure in which the subject receives the action expressed by the verb.
use_cases: The cat was chased by the dog. (passive voice)
The letter was written by her. (passive, often used when the doer is unknown or less important)

definition: A group of words containing a subject and a verb; can be independent (main) or dependent (subordinate).
use_cases: She laughed. (independent clause)
Although it was raining, they went outside. (dependent clause + independent clause)

definition: A group of words functioning as a unit in a sentence but lacking a subject-verb combination.
use_cases: In the morning (prepositional phrase)
Running quickly (participial phrase modifying the subject)

definition: The noun, pronoun, or noun phrase that performs the action or is described in the sentence.
use_cases: John runs. (John is the subject)
The big red apple fell. (The big red apple is the subject)

definition: The part of the sentence that tells something about the subject, including the verb.
use_cases: The dog barked loudly. (barked loudly is the predicate)
She is happy. (is happy is the predicate)

definition: A noun or pronoun that receives the action of a transitive verb.
use_cases: She kicked the ball. (ball is the direct object)
He read the book. (book is the direct object)

definition: A noun or pronoun that indicates to whom or for whom the action is done.
use_cases: She gave him a gift. (him is the indirect object)
I told my friend the news. (my friend is the indirect object)

definition: A word or phrase that completes the meaning of the subject, object, or verb.
use_cases: She is a teacher. (teacher is a subject complement)
They elected him president. (president is an object complement)

definition: A word, phrase, or clause that describes or limits another word.
use_cases: The extremely tall building (extremely modifies tall; tall modifies building)
She arrived late. (late modifies arrived)

definition: A word that describes or modifies a noun or pronoun.
use_cases: The blue sky (blue modifies sky)
He is happy. (happy modifies he)

definition: A word that modifies a verb, adjective, or another adverb, often telling how, when, where, or to what extent.
use_cases: She runs quickly. (quickly modifies runs)
Very bright (very modifies bright)

definition: A word that shows the relationship between a noun/pronoun and another word.
use_cases: On the table (on shows relationship)
Through the tunnel (through shows relationship)

definition: A word that connects words, phrases, or clauses.
use_cases: And, but, or (coordinating)
Because, although (subordinating)

definition: A word or phrase expressing emotion, often standing alone.
use_cases: Wow! (surprise)
Ouch! That hurts. (pain)

definition: A sentence with one independent clause.
use_cases: Birds fly.
The quick brown fox jumps.

definition: A sentence with two or more independent clauses joined by a coordinating conjunction.
use_cases: I wanted to go, but it rained.
She studied hard, and she passed the exam.

definition: A sentence with one independent clause and at least one dependent clause.
use_cases: Although he was tired, he finished the work.
She smiled when she saw the gift.

definition: A sentence with at least two independent clauses and one or more dependent clauses.
use_cases: Although it was raining, we went to the park, and we had fun.
When the bell rang, the students left, but some stayed to ask questions.

definition: A sentence that makes a statement.
use_cases: The sky is blue.
I enjoy reading books.

definition: A sentence that asks a question.
use_cases: What time is it?
Are you coming to the party?

definition: A sentence that gives a command or request.
use_cases: Close the door.
Please pass the salt.

definition: A sentence that expresses strong emotion.
use_cases: What a beautiful day!
I can't believe it!

definition: An incomplete sentence lacking a subject, verb, or complete thought.
use_cases: Running down the street. (fragment)
Because it was raining. (dependent clause fragment)

definition: Two or more independent clauses incorrectly joined without proper punctuation or conjunction.
use_cases: I love pizza it's my favorite food. (run-on)
She ran to the store, she bought milk.

definition: A type of run-on where two independent clauses are joined only by a comma.
use_cases: It was cold, I wore a jacket. (comma splice)
He studied hard, he passed the test.

definition: A modifier that does not clearly refer to the word it is intended to modify.
use_cases: Walking down the street, the trees were beautiful. (dangling; who is walking?)
Correct: Walking down the street, I saw beautiful trees.

definition: A modifier placed in a position that causes confusion about what it modifies.
use_cases: She almost drove her kids to school every day. (implies almost drove but didn't)
Correct: She drove her kids to school almost every day.

definition: Using the same grammatical form for items in a list or comparison.
use_cases: She likes hiking, swimming, and biking. (parallel)
Not parallel: She likes hiking, to swim, and bike.

definition: The subject and verb must agree in number (singular/plural).
use_cases: The dog barks. (singular)
The dogs bark. (plural)
Everyone is here. (singular indefinite pronoun)

definition: A pronoun must agree with its antecedent in number, gender, and person.
use_cases: Each student must bring his or her book. (singular)
The team celebrated their victory. (often accepted in modern usage)

definition: The form of the verb that indicates time (past, present, future).
use_cases: I walk (present)
I walked (past)
I will walk (future)

definition: Indicates whether an action is complete, ongoing, or repeated (simple, progressive, perfect).
use_cases: She eats (simple present)
She is eating (present progressive)
She has eaten (present perfect)

definition: Indicates the attitude of the speaker (indicative, imperative, subjunctive).
use_cases: He runs. (indicative)
Run! (imperative)
If I were rich... (subjunctive)

definition: A noun or noun phrase that renames or explains another noun beside it.
use_cases: My brother, a doctor, is coming. (a doctor renames brother)
The capital city, Washington D.C., is beautiful.

definition: A verb form ending in -ing that functions as a noun.
use_cases: Swimming is fun. (subject)
I enjoy reading. (object)

definition: A verb form used as an adjective (present: -ing, past: -ed or irregular).
use_cases: The running water (present participle)
Broken glass (past participle)

definition: The base form of the verb, often preceded by 'to'.
use_cases: To err is human. (subject)
I want to go. (object)

definition: Joining equal grammatical elements with coordinating conjunctions (FANBOYS: for, and, nor, but, or, yet, so).
use_cases: I called, but no one answered.
She is smart and kind.

definition: Joining a dependent clause to an independent clause using subordinating conjunctions.
use_cases: Because it rained, we stayed inside.
I'll go if you go.

definition: The arrangement of words and phrases to create well-formed sentences.
use_cases: Understanding syntax helps in analyzing complex sentences.
Poor syntax can make writing unclear.

definition: The study of meaning in language.
use_cases: The semantics of 'bank' changes: river bank vs. money bank.
Misunderstanding semantics leads to confusion.

definition: The study of how context influences the interpretation of language.
use_cases: 'Can you pass the salt?' is pragmatically a request, not a question about ability.
Sarcasm relies on pragmatics.

definition: Language that uses figures of speech, not literal meaning.
use_cases: It's raining cats and dogs. (idiom)
Her smile was a ray of sunshine. (metaphor)

definition: A direct comparison between unlike things without using like or as.
use_cases: Time is a thief.
The world is a stage.

definition: A comparison using like or as.
use_cases: Brave as a lion.
She sings like an angel.

definition: Giving human qualities to non-human things.
use_cases: The wind whispered through the trees.
Time flies.

definition: An indirect reference to something well-known.
use_cases: He met his Waterloo. (allusion to Napoleon's defeat)
She's a real Cinderella story.

definition: A contrast between expectation and reality.
use_cases: A fire station burns down. (situational irony)
'Great weather,' he said during the storm. (verbal irony)

definition: The author's attitude toward the subject or audience.
use_cases: The tone was sarcastic.
A formal tone in academic writing.

definition: The distinctive style or personality of the writing; also active/passive.
use_cases: Hemingway's voice is concise and direct.
Use active voice for clarity.

definition: The central idea or message in a literary work, often exploring universal human experiences.
use_cases: The theme of revenge drives Hamlet.
Common themes include love, loss, and redemption.

definition: A recurring element, image, or idea that has symbolic significance and helps develop the theme.
use_cases: The motif of blood in Macbeth represents guilt.
Birds as a motif often symbolize freedom.

definition: The use of symbols to represent ideas or qualities beyond their literal meaning.
use_cases: The green light in The Great Gatsby symbolizes Gatsby's dreams.
A dove often symbolizes peace.

definition: A literary device where the author gives hints or clues about events that will occur later.
use_cases: The storm foreshadowed the tragic ending.
His ominous warning foreshadowed danger.

definition: An interruption in the chronological narrative to show past events.
use_cases: The story used a flashback to reveal her childhood.
He experienced a flashback to the war.

definition: The perspective from which the story is told (first-person, third-person limited, third-person omniscient).
use_cases: First-person: 'I ran home.'
Third-person omniscient knows all characters' thoughts.

definition: The voice or character telling the story.
use_cases: An unreliable narrator distorts the truth.
The omniscient narrator revealed everyone's secrets.

definition: The main character around whom the story revolves, often facing conflict.
use_cases: Harry Potter is the protagonist of the series.
The protagonist overcame great obstacles.

definition: The character or force that opposes the protagonist.
use_cases: Voldemort is Harry's antagonist.
The antagonist can be nature or society, not just a person.

definition: The methods an author uses to reveal a character's personality (direct or indirect).
use_cases: Direct: 'She was kind.'
Indirect: shown through actions, thoughts, dialogue.

definition: A simple, one-dimensional character with few traits.
use_cases: Minor characters are often flat.
The wicked stepmother is a flat villain.

definition: A complex, multi-dimensional character with depth and contradictions.
use_cases: Elizabeth Bennet is a round character.
Round characters feel realistic and change over time.

definition: A character who undergoes significant internal change.
use_cases: Ebenezer Scrooge is dynamic; he becomes generous.
The protagonist often develops dynamically.

definition: A character who remains the same throughout the story.
use_cases: Sherlock Holmes is largely static.
Static characters provide consistency.

definition: The central struggle between opposing forces in a story.
use_cases: Man vs. man, man vs. self, man vs. nature.
Internal conflict: guilt over a decision.

definition: The sequence of events in a story, typically following exposition, rising action, climax, falling action, resolution.
use_cases: The plot twisted unexpectedly.
Freytag's pyramid outlines classic plot structure.

definition: The beginning of the story that provides background information.
use_cases: The exposition introduced the setting and characters.
Too much exposition can slow the pace.

definition: Events that build tension and complicate the conflict leading to the climax.
use_cases: Complications arise in the rising action.
Suspense builds during rising action.

definition: The turning point or moment of highest tension in the story.
use_cases: The duel was the climax of the novel.
The climax resolves the main conflict.

definition: Events after the climax that lead toward resolution.
use_cases: Consequences unfold in the falling action.
The falling action ties up subplots.

definition: The conclusion where conflicts are resolved and loose ends tied.
use_cases: The resolution provided a happy ending.
Some stories have open-ended resolutions.

definition: The time, place, and environment in which the story occurs.
use_cases: The setting was Victorian London.
Setting can influence mood and character.

definition: The emotional atmosphere created by the author's word choice and description.
use_cases: The dark forest created a moody of fear.
Music in films helps establish mood.

definition: The author's attitude toward the subject, conveyed through word choice and style.
use_cases: The tone was ironic and mocking.
A satirical tone critiques society.

definition: A story with a hidden moral or political meaning; characters and events represent abstract ideas.
use_cases: Animal Farm is an allegory for the Russian Revolution.
Pilgrim's Progress is a Christian allegory.

definition: The use of humor, irony, or exaggeration to criticize flaws in society or individuals.
use_cases: The Onion uses satire for news.
Swift's A Modest Proposal is biting satire.

definition: Deliberate exaggeration for emphasis or humor.
use_cases: I'm so hungry I could eat a horse.
His bag weighs a ton.

definition: Presenting something as less important than it is for ironic or emphatic effect.
use_cases: 'It's just a scratch' said about a huge wound.
British humor often uses understatement.

definition: A figure of speech combining contradictory terms.
use_cases: Jumbo shrimp
Deafening silence

definition: A statement that seems contradictory but reveals a truth.
use_cases: Less is more.
The beginning of the end.

definition: Repetition of initial consonant sounds in neighboring words.
use_cases: Peter Piper picked a peck...
She sells seashells.

definition: Repetition of vowel sounds in nearby words.
use_cases: The rain in Spain stays mainly in the plain.
Fleet feet sweep by sleeping geese.

definition: Repetition of consonant sounds, typically at the end of words.
use_cases: Pitter-patter
Blank and think

definition: Words that imitate the sound they represent.
use_cases: Buzz, crash, splash
The bees buzzed.

definition: Correspondence of sound between words or endings of words.
use_cases: Cat and hat rhyme.
End rhyme in poetry.

definition: The rhythmic pattern of stressed and unstressed syllables in poetry.
use_cases: Iambic pentameter: da-DUM x5
Shakespeare often used iambic pentameter.

definition: A grouped set of lines in a poem, separated by space.
use_cases: A quatrain is a four-line stanza.
Sonnets have specific stanza patterns.

definition: A 14-line poem, typically in iambic pentameter, with specific rhyme schemes (Shakespearean or Petrarchan).
use_cases: Shakespeare's sonnets explore love.
Sonnet 18: 'Shall I compare thee to a summer's day?'

definition: Poetry without consistent rhyme or meter.
use_cases: Walt Whitman wrote in free verse.
Modern poetry often uses free verse.

definition: Vivid descriptive language that appeals to the senses.
use_cases: Visual imagery of a crimson rose.
Tactile imagery of rough bark.

definition: The continuation of a sentence without a pause beyond the end of a line in poetry.
use_cases: The thought runs over / into the next line.
Creates flow and tension.

definition: A pause within a line of poetry, often marked by punctuation.
use_cases: To be || or not to be
Creates dramatic pause.

definition: A category of literature characterized by style, form, or content (e.g., fiction, poetry, drama).
use_cases: Science fiction is a popular genre.
Mystery novels belong to the detective genre.

definition: A long work of narrative prose fiction.
use_cases: Pride and Prejudice is a classic novel.
Modern novels vary widely in style.

definition: A work of prose fiction longer than a short story but shorter than a novel.
use_cases: The Old Man and the Sea is a novella.
Animal Farm is sometimes classified as a novella.

definition: A brief work of prose fiction, usually with a single focused plot.
use_cases: Edgar Allan Poe wrote famous short stories.
O. Henry's stories often have twist endings.

definition: A work intended for performance, written in dialogue form.
use_cases: Romeo and Juliet is a drama.
Modern drama includes plays by Tennessee Williams.

definition: A drama depicting serious events leading to a disastrous or sorrowful conclusion, often involving a heroic figure's downfall.
use_cases: Oedipus Rex is a classic tragedy.
Hamlet is a Shakespearean tragedy.

definition: A drama that ends happily, often involving humor and misunderstandings.
use_cases: A Midsummer Night's Dream is a comedy.
Modern romantic comedies follow similar patterns.
